A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFRO study and contain complete, readable main text, six tables, ten figures, and Appendices A–F. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original AFRO experiments on 16 simulated and four real-world manipulation tasks, including baseline comparisons, scaling studies, generalization tests, and ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation and real-robot results, including the complete per-task results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same feature-differencing inverse dynamics, inverse-consistency supervision, diffusion-based forward dynamics, EMA encoder, and VICReg objective. No algorithmic or architectural changes appear.

E1.justification: Both versions use two Adroit tasks, fourteen MetaWorld tasks, four Franka tasks, and the same RH20T subset. Object-transfer and cluttered-scene evaluation coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the tables and analyses. DynaMo and DynaMo-3D already appear in v3; correcting their bibliographic reference in v4 does not introduce or revise an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, hyperparameters, demonstration counts, preprocessing, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. The existing difference between the 25-rollout description in Section 5.3 and the 50-rollout description in Appendix D persists in both versions.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same data/domain scaling studies, t-SNE analysis, object and clutter generalization tests, component ablations, and appendix rollout visualizations. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 6 and Appendix D retain the same reporting of best success over unspecified multiple runs. No seed information, run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Tables 1–6 and the scaling plots. AFRO still reports 76.0% mean MetaWorld success, 83.0% Adroit success, and 70%/84% real-world success with in-domain/out-of-domain pretraining.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the associated mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about action-free, reconstruction-free 3D representation learning, latent-action novelty, manipulation performance, and scalability.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning pretraining scale, semantic coverage, single-view inputs, latent-action interpretability, and dependence on VICReg.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, RH20T processing instructions, and 1024-point sampling remain identical. The project-page address is unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v4 supplies the previously missing bibliography entry for Cui et al.'s DynaMo as reference [9], replacing v3's duplicate DINOv2 entry [30] that the DynaMo passages cited. This changes the cited source, while the existing DynaMo discussion and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the corrected bibliography entry, corresponding citation renumbering, and the arXiv version/date stamp. Main-text and appendix prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: The reference correction reflows the bibliography across pages 9–11 and slightly changes Table 1 spacing. All figures, table structures, captions, and scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3's DynaMo citations in Section 2.2 and Table 1 point to a duplicate DINOv2 reference. v4 supplies the matching DynaMo source, improving attribution and readers' ability to locate this baseline. The benefit is limited: the methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, and limitations are unchanged.
